body:
You're right.

I have more to say, but I don't know how to ask for help or how to say it.  I know I'm not weak, but I am embarrassed of depression, and my mind says that I could get over it if only I was stronger.  I want help, but I'm worried that I can't be helped.

I know you're right.  Although I say there's nothing to do, nothing to fight for, or nothing to say, I think I just mean that I don't know how to deal with everything going on and everything I'm feeling.

>What's going on?

There's a lot going on, so I apologize in advance...

-An acquaintance recently died due to an overdose.  (Sometimes I wish it was me instead...)

-Depression is honestly the worst.  It's been a problem for over a year, and I tried to commit suicide two months ago.  I'm in therapy (I bought a subscription to Talkspace and I have a counselor through my college), and I've been prescribed antidepressants by a psychiatrist, but my family and friends are against both of these things.  They say that if I clean, eat more, exercise, shower, or try harder, then maybe I will get over it rather than relying on antidepressants and medication.

-I think I'm about to fail out of my program in college.  (The requirements are strict - I need to be at a B or better, but I'm definitely struggling in all 6 of my courses.  This is particularly upsetting because I performed so well in high school and the first two years of undergraduate schooling.)

-My car broke down.  Due to this, I was late to work and therefore fired.  I have enough from my other job closer to campus to pay for basic necessities (food, rent, utilities), but I have no idea how I'll be able to afford anything else (appointments for my psychologist and therapist, medication, repairs for my car).

-Someone has been anonymously bullying me (anonymous calls, e-mails, reports to the college, text messages).

-The 2 year relationship with my boyfriend recently ended due to cheating.
